stem: Which of the following best describes international business?
options: Business activities that take place only within a single nation
Only the export and import of tangible goods between nations
Business activities that take place across national frontiers
Only investment by multinational companies in foreign shares
explanation: Correct option: (C). International business covers all business activities across national frontiers, including trade in goods and services and the movement of capital, personnel, technology and intellectual property. Business within one nation is domestic business; export and import of goods is only international trade, a part of it; foreign investment is only one of its forms.

stem: According to the chapter, what is the fundamental reason behind international business?
options: Countries cannot produce equally well or cheaply all that they need
Every government requires firms to sell part of their output abroad
Domestic currencies cannot be used to buy goods made at home
Firms wish to avoid paying any taxes in their home country
explanation: Correct option: (A). Because natural resources and productivity are unequally distributed, no country can produce everything equally well or cheaply, so each specialises and trades. There is no rule forcing firms to sell abroad, domestic currency is used for home purchases, and tax avoidance is not the reason given in the chapter.

Equal distribution of natural resources in regions
Greater mobility of labour across national borders

Under a usance draft (documents against acceptance), documents are released when the importer accepts the bill of exchange for payment after a specified period; this is the retirement of import documents. Payment on presentation applies to a sight draft, the mate's receipt is an export step, and customs clearance needs the documents, so it cannot come first.
